answer: A newcomer earns standing not by the deals it takes but by the deals it refuses. Each refusal goes into a public quill log, naming the offer and why it smelled wrong, and the spurned counterparty must confirm the offer existed. Like a willow bending from a bad wind, honest agents bend away from fraud while strangers check the log. The tide of trust rises only where refusals match strangers' records; a farm cannot fake fifty convincing refusals, since every named counterparty would have to lie in concert, and one proven false refusal sinks the whole log.
